paper.citation: Gilchrist, C. L. M., Mirdita, M., Steinegger, M. Multiple protein structure alignment at scale with FoldMason. Science 391(6784):485-488 (2026)
paper.preprint: bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.08.01.606130 (v3, 2024-08-27; a different, earlier analysis: 150 AFDB clusters, older FoldMason commit; not used for any value here)

paper_text_access: Not readable from this machine on 2026-10-27. science.org returns HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) for the article and its supplement; Europe PMC has the abstract only (isOpenAccess N, no PMC copy); bioRxiv returned HTTP 429 / Cloudflare error 1015 for the preprint full text; the Seoul National University repository copy (hdl.handle.net/10371/231064, found via OpenAlex) sits behind a JavaScript bot check. None of these checks were bypassed. As a result no claimed value below could be read from the printed paper, Fig. 2 or Tables S1/S2. Every value was derived from the authors' released per-family score tables with the aggregation in their own FoldMason_benchmarks.R (scripts/summarise_author_scores.py, output sources/author_scores_summary.txt). A human with Science access should check the values against Fig. 2 and the supplement before the report is published.

claims.quantity: HOMSTRAD full set, FoldMason (default mode), mean sum-of-pairs score, forward direction (sp_fwd)
claims.location: Fig. 2A, panel 'HOMSTRAD Full', FoldMason point, y axis (labelled 'Specificity (%)' in the authors' R script)
claims.value_status: derived from the authors' per-family scores, not confirmed in the paper text (90.014466 = mean of 1030 per-family sp_fwd values in data/homstrad_scores.tsv)
claims.tolerance_basis: 1 standard error of the mean of the authors' own 1030 per-family sp_fwd values (sd 12.1617 / sqrt(1030)). FoldMason is deterministic in default mode, so with identical inputs and t_coffee the expected difference is below 0.01; anything between 0.01 and 0.379 is reported as 'within tolerance, not exact' and the per-family differences are listed.
claims.conditions: FoldMason release 4-dd3c235, foldmason easy-msa <family>/pdbs out tmp --threads 1; reference MSA from HOMSTRAD homstrad_with_PDB_2024_Dec_1 processed by clean_homstrad.py; families with count >= 2 in data/homstrad_families.tsv (1030 of 1032); score = t_coffee -other_pg aln_compare -al1 <HOMSTRAD ref> -al2 <foldmason_aa.fa> -compare_mode sp. Runs only if the HOMSTRAD release can be obtained (server down since 2026-05, issue #38); otherwise status 'could not run'.

definitions.name: Software version
definitions.choice: FoldMason release 4-dd3c235 (commit dd3c23500ce0893bc1b5f9b4a3e17c63796a5d0b), prebuilt foldmason-linux-avx2.tar.gz from the GitHub release, checked against the release size; the same binary computes the LDDT (msa2lddtreport). Not the current main (b4fa299, 7 commits later, with lolalign and two-pass contacts).
definitions.quote: Paper text not accessible. The authors' scripts call whatever 'foldmason' is on PATH: "[foldmason]=$(command -v "foldmason")" (align_family.sh).
definitions.ambiguity: The release (2025-10-08) and the analysis data commit (2025-10-10) are two days apart, and nothing states that the released TSVs were produced with exactly this binary. Triage (not the paper) links the Science version to 4-dd3c235 via Zenodo 17315302. If the default-mode HOMSTRAD scores match per family to 1e-6, that settles it; if they do not, the version is the first suspect and the report says so.

definitions.name: HOMSTRAD input data
definitions.choice: homstrad_with_PDB_2024_Dec_1.tar.gz, with the authors' igV chain-order fix, split into one PDB per member plus <family>_msa.fasta (reference MSA) and sequence.fa by clean_homstrad.py, unmodified. First look inside the Zenodo 17311030 tarball for a homstrad folder; if neither it nor an identical copy of the Dec 2024 release can be found, C1-C4 and S1-S5 are 'could not run'. A different HOMSTRAD release is not a substitute.
definitions.ambiguity: Server unreachable since 2026-05 (issue #38). download_homstrad.sh writes to homstrad_clean2 while the README says homstrad_clean; only the folder name differs. clean_homstrad.py hard-codes sequence replacements for 1ka5a, 1pi2 and 1m85a; keep them.

definitions.name: HOMSTRAD family set (full)
definitions.choice: Families with count >= 2 in data/homstrad_families.tsv: 1030 of 1032. Tool rows only (the 'homstrad' reference row has no SP rows).
definitions.ambiguity: The R filter compares against "Homstrad" while name_map produces "HOMSTRAD", so that clause excludes nothing; harmless because the reference has no sp rows in the TSV (checked: tools with sp rows are the 15 aligners only). Decided from the authors' released TSV.

definitions.name: HOMSTRAD hard subset
definitions.choice: Exactly the 55 family names listed in homstrad.hard of FoldMason_benchmarks.R. We do not recompute identity or membership.
definitions.ambiguity: How identity was computed is not in the code; using the authors' list removes the question. All 55 pass the count >= 2 filter (n = 55 in the authors' TSV).

definitions.name: Sum-of-pairs score and its two directions
definitions.choice: sp_fwd = t_coffee -other_pg aln_compare -al1 <ref> -al2 <test> -compare_mode sp, field 4 of output line 3; sp_rev = same with -al1/-al2 swapped. Per family, 0-100 scale. t_coffee from Ubuntu 24.04 apt; version recorded.
definitions.ambiguity: The authors' t_coffee version is not stated. The labels disagree inside the R script: the comment calls one direction specificity and the other accuracy, Fig. 2A plots sp_fwd on the y axis as 'Specificity (%)' and sp_rev on x as 'Sensitivity (%)', while Fig. S3 labels sp_fwd 'Sensitivity' and sp_rev 'Specificity'. We report by command direction (fwd/rev) and do not rely on the words.

definitions.name: FoldMason runs and output used
definitions.choice: Default: foldmason easy-msa <family>/pdbs <family>/foldmason <family>/foldmason_tmp --threads 1, scored on foldmason_aa.fa. Fast: same plus --fast, scored on foldmason_fast_aa.fa. No other flag. Not in scope: R100 (--refine-iters 100 --refine-seed 858702543) and R100 OSC.
definitions.quote: "easy-msa \"$PDB\" \"${1}/foldmason\" \"${1}/foldmason_tmp\" --threads $THREADS" (align_family.sh; THREADS defaults to 1 via TOOL_THREADS=1 in align_families.sh)
definitions.ambiguity: Single-thread is the authors' setting. Running up to 4 families in parallel (light mode) does not change any single run. The PDB folder is passed as a directory, so file names and directory order are inputs (issue #35: renaming files changed the LDDT from 0.741 to 0.724 in one example); keep the authors' file names.

definitions.name: HOMSTRAD aggregation
definitions.choice: Plain mean over families of the per-family score, per tool and direction, for the full set (D3) and hard set (D4). F1 = 2*mean_fwd*mean_rev/(mean_fwd+mean_rev) on those means.
definitions.ambiguity: In Fig. 2A the label 'FoldMason R100' is the refine100 run scored with only-scoring-cols refinement (foldmason_refine100_rosc renamed), and plain refine100 is dropped; this does not touch the FoldMason and FoldMason Fast claims.

definitions.name: AFDB cluster set
definitions.choice: The 200 clusters of data/afdb_families.tsv (identical to afdb_clusters/final_clusters.tsv): 50 each with 1, 2, 3 and 4 domains, 20 member accessions each (checked in the file). Remove the 40 accessions in afdb.training: 160 clusters, 40 per domain count.
definitions.quote: "# 40 clusters used for parameter optimisation, removed for benchmark" (FoldMason_benchmarks.R)
definitions.ambiguity: afdb_clusters/README.md and extract_clusters.awk speak of 2, 3 and 4-domain clusters, but the released list also has 50 one-domain clusters (awk filter is $4 <= 4). We follow the released list, which is what the authors' scores cover.

definitions.name: AFDB structures
definitions.choice: For each member, download AF-<acc>-F1-model_v6.pdb (v4 now returns 404) and save it as AF-<acc>-F1-model_v4.pdb in <cluster>/pdbs/, the name the authors' download.sh produces. Check each download against the server Content-Length. Record, per member, whether the v6 sequence/length equals what the authors' run saw where that can be checked (e.g. against v4 files if any are found in Zenodo afdb_scaling/pdbs.tar.gz, or sequence.fa if released).
definitions.ambiguity: This is a forced input change, not a method change, and the report must say so. v6 coordinates can differ from v4, so per-cluster LDDT can move. Triage suggested checking lengths against data/afdb_lengths.tsv, but that file holds per-tool MSA lengths (family, tool, length), not structure lengths, so it can only be compared after alignment and does not isolate the input change.

definitions.name: LDDT metric
definitions.choice: foldmason msa2lddtreport <cluster>/foldmason_tmp/latest/structures <msa> <out>.html --threads 1, value = the msaLDDT field parsed by extractLDDT.awk. Full-MSA LDDT (no --only-scoring-cols) for all claims. Both default and Fast MSAs are scored against the structure DB written by the default run.
definitions.ambiguity: Fig. 2B uses the non-OSC values (line_test_data filters !osc), the OSC variant appears in Fig. S6. The OSC numbers (0.6480, 0.6476) are not claims here. Issue #20 reports 'Found nan' in msa2lddtreport; any NaN cluster is reported, not dropped silently (the authors' TSV has 160 finite values per tool).

definitions.name: AFDB aggregation
definitions.choice: C5/C6: plain mean of per-cluster LDDT over the 160 clusters. S6-S10: plain mean within each num_domains group (40 clusters each), which is what Fig. 2B plots as 'Average'.
definitions.ambiguity: Fig. 2B itself does not plot the 160-cluster mean; that number comes from afdb.summary (avg_lddt). Which printed table carries it could not be checked (paper inaccessible).

definitions.name: Scoring script defects to handle without changing the method
definitions.choice: compute_scores.sh calls apply_fn compute_nirmsd, a function that is not defined; under bash -e that aborts after the SP block on HOMSTRAD families. The run stage may skip that call (environment/crash fix, logged in patches/). TC and CS are written as 0 by the script and are not claims.
definitions.ambiguity: Removing the call does not change any SP or LDDT value; it only lets the script reach the LDDT/time extraction.

out_of_scope: Other aligners (3DCoffee, US-align, mTM-align, MUSTANG, Matt, Caretta, MAFFT, MAFFT-3Di, MUSCLE, FAMSA2, Clustal Omega): not rerun. Their published MSAs may be rescored later only as a check of our scoring setup, not as claims.
FoldMason R100 and OSC values, runtimes and speedups (machine-dependent), Fig. 2C scaling, Fig. 2D flexible proteins, glycoprotein trees.
Any number from the bioRxiv preprint (different analysis).
